dedupe_keys.name: comparison of online static gnss post processing services opus s auspos csrs ppp gaps trimble rtx

description: This testbed study compared the accuracy of five free online services for post-processing static GNSS data on a survey mark: OPUS-S from the US National Geodetic Survey, AUSPOS from Geoscience Australia, CSRS-PPP from Natural Resources Canada, GAPS from the University of New Brunswick and Trimble RTX. Marian Jamieson of Oregon State University and Daniel Gillins, later of NGS, processed the same 490 static GPS files of 2 to 10 hours, recorded on six passive marks in minimal and moderate multipath environments, and compared the results with coordinates from a high-accuracy campaign survey. With GPS-only data at 30-second logging, all five services gave similar results: for sessions of five hours or more, horizontal and vertical root-mean-square errors differed by less than 1 cm between services, and hardly improved beyond about 2 cm after three and five hours at the two kinds of site. Logging at 10 instead of 30 seconds did not reduce errors, but adding GLONASS observations in Trimble RTX and CSRS-PPP cut horizontal errors by 17.1 per cent and 36.7 per cent on average at minimal and moderate multipath sites. The authors preferred CSRS-PPP for batch processing, advised surveyors to use several services for high-accuracy work, and warned of AUSPOS solutions with very large reported errors. Coverage: six marks in Oregon, United States. Format and access: accepted manuscript in the NOAA Institutional Repository, free. Caveats: one region and older service versions; services have since added constellations. Simulation uses: accuracy assumptions for asset positions in digital twins and hazard maps. Related records: OPUS, AUSPOS and CSRS-PPP are recorded as services.
